Java lookup scans visible immediate declarations in ancestor scopes; for C calls and S declarations worst-case O(C*S), as the old method-descendant search already was. The new lexical scan avoids nested unrelated method/body traversal; no new repository-wide scan. No claim of globally linear extraction.
Outgoing call-site object assembly adds O(1) per returned edge and reuses existing per-file call scans; context source attribution adds O(returned rows). No new corpus scans or file reads.

Explicit offline census runs eight fixed aggregate queries within one read transaction and closes in finally, including errors. Group/order/count-distinct SQL may require O(E log E) temp work and malformed-target detail can be O(E) output. Appropriate for explicit census, not a warmed MCP read; no new query-time invocation introduced.
